claims.quote: Administer intramuscular epinephrine into the anterolateral thigh as the first-line treatment of anaphylaxis.
Epinephrine is the cornerstone of treatment for anaphylaxis; it may help relieve all symptoms and signs and should be given immediately

claims.text: IM into the anterolateral thigh is the preferred route
claims.quote: intramuscular administration into the anterolateral thigh is the preferred route.

claims.text: MOA: ↑ peripheral vascular resistance + inotropic/chronotropic effects → ↑ BP; bronchodilation; ↓ mucosal edema; stabilizes mast cells and basophils
claims.quote: Epinephrine causes an increase in peripheral vascular resistance plus inotropic and chronotropic cardiac effects, leading to an increase in blood pressure. It causes bronchodilation and decreased mucosal edema through the vasodilation of the skeletal and smooth muscles in the airways and stabilization of mast cells and basophils.

claims.text: Dose: 0.3–0.5 mL of 1:1000 (0.1%) in adults, 0.01 mL/kg in children; repeat q5–15 min
claims.quote: The usual dose of parenteral epinephrine is 0.3 to 0.5 mL of a 1:1000 [0.1%] solution in adults or 0.01 mL/kg in children, repeated every 5 to 15 minutes.

claims.text: Onset usually three to five minutes
claims.quote: The onset of action of epinephrine is usually three to five minutes

claims.text: Hypotension or severe airway obstruction: IV or IO (continuous drip preferred)
claims.quote: Patients with hypotension or severe airway obstruction may be given epinephrine IV or intraosseously (IO). A continuous drip using an infusion pump is preferred

claims.text: Intranasal epinephrine may be an alternative where available
claims.quote: Intranasal epinephrine may be an alternative in health care settings where it is available.
in patients aged ≥ 4 years who weigh ≥ 15 kg.

claims.text: Give it even if the pt takes a beta-blocker
claims.quote: because epinephrine is the most effective therapy for anaphylaxis, it should be used regardless of beta-blocker therapy.

claims.text: AEs: agitation, anxiety, tremulousness, HA, dizziness, pallor, palpitations; no absolute contraindications in anaphylaxis
claims.quote: At recommended doses, the most common adverse effects of epinephrine include agitation, anxiety, tremulousness, headache, dizziness, pallor, and palpitations. There are no absolute contraindications to administering epinephrine for anaphylaxis.

claims.text: Prescribe an auto-injector (0.3 mg adults, 0.15 mg children)
claims.quote: carry a prefilled, self-injecting epinephrine syringe (containing 0.3 mg for adults and 0.15 mg for children)

claims.text: and an action plan to every pt at risk
claims.quote: Prescribe auto-injectable epinephrine to all patients at risk for an anaphylactic reaction, and provide an action plan
